observational_variants.rationale: upgrade-boundary: not feature-gated. Journals the split gateway's activation-time flow selection so completion takes exactly those flows instead of re-evaluating FEEL. The state it writes (Instance::gateway_routes, serde(default)) is transient - cleared when the gateway completes - and a gateway completing without a recorded selection re-selects from the current variables exactly as the previous release does, so the routed flows (SequenceFlowTaken, compared unfiltered) agree on both builds. But Raft members RE-EXECUTE committed commands (ADR 0066, Rolling upgrade, option C): a previous-release member neither emits this event nor can decode it, so a mixed-version cluster journals different events for the same command. The release therefore requires an all-nodes-same-version (quiesced) upgrade; no rolling upgrade across it.

divergences.rationale: upgrade-boundary: not feature-gated. Zeebe execution order at forks and joins (#1244, PR #1428): a parallel fork now activates its branches in Zeebe's order, so the branch elements' keys are minted in a different order (reorder + remint_keys), and a parallel join activates its element instance when it FIRES rather than on the first arriving token (the join's ElementActivating/ElementActivated move from the first token's entry to the firing entry, which only_in_prev/only_in_head declare for element `join` alone). Every other event - flows taken, subscriptions, variables, completions - is unchanged. Raft members RE-EXECUTE committed commands (ADR 0066, Rolling upgrade, option C) rather than replay the leader's events, so previous-release and new members would mint different keys and journal different events for the same command. The new order is not gated on a cluster-wide capability, so the release requires an all-nodes-same-version (quiesced) upgrade; no rolling upgrade across it.

upgrade-boundary: not feature-gated. Zeebe parity (#1535): an activity interrupted by an interrupting boundary event or event sub-process now TERMINATES (ElementTerminating/ElementTerminated) instead of COMPLETING (ElementCompleting/ElementCompleted) - completion implies the activity finished its work and takes its outgoing flows, termination is the interrupt. In this scenario the interrupting timer boundary on the `slow` task fires, so prev journals the task's completion pair where head journals the termination pair; the boundary event, its outgoing flow and every other event are unchanged (only_in_prev/only_in_head reconcile the substitution per element instance at scenario level). Raft members RE-EXECUTE committed commands (ADR 0066, Rolling upgrade, option C): a previous-release member journals the completion pair where a new member journals termination, so a mixed-version cluster diverges for the same command. The release therefore requires an all-nodes-same-version (quiesced) upgrade; no rolling upgrade across it. Additionally (#1712, Zeebe parity): a TriggerTimers batch now fires its due timers ONE AT A TIME in key order, each drained to completion before the next (Zeebe writes one TIMER TRIGGER command per due timer), so in this scenario the three `wait` catches' completions and the `slow` activations/jobs/boundary timers interleave per timer instead of all TimerTriggered events preceding all follow-ups (reorder). Element instances created by the follow-ups (`tb`, `timed-out`) are therefore minted in a different order (remint_keys); the multiset of events is otherwise unchanged. This is likewise not feature-gated: a previous-release member journals the batch-first order where a new member journals per-trigger order for the same command, so the same all-nodes-same-version (quiesced) upgrade is required.

upgrade-boundary: not feature-gated. Ad-hoc sub-process activation (#1632) now records the real enclosing scope on ElementActivating for a tool's `<container>#innerInstance` and its tool child (the container's element-instance key), where the previous release's journal carries no `ElementActivating.scope` field and decodes it to the serde default `0`. The field is golden-recorded as added since the previous release, so it is erased from both sides where it holds the default; here head populates it, a one-field behavioural refinement declared as a field_overrides normalization to `0` on both sides. Every other event - the activation, the job, the completion - is unchanged. Raft members RE-EXECUTE committed commands (ADR 0066, Rolling upgrade, option C): a previous-release member journals `scope: 0` (absent) where a new member journals the real scope, so a mixed-version cluster journals different events for the same command. The release therefore requires an all-nodes-same-version (quiesced) upgrade; no rolling upgrade across it.
